corrected_value.authors: Gailliot, M. T., Baumeister, R. F., DeWall, C. N., Maner, J. K., Plant, E. A., Tice, D. M., et al.
corrected_value.title: Self-control relies on glucose as a limited energy source. Willpower is more than a metaphor.

decisions.location: Experiment 1, p. 56 (line 229); Experiment 1 Discussion, p. 58 (line 361); Experiment 2 Discussion, p. 61 (line 559); General discussion, pp. 61-62 (lines 569, 575); References, p. 62 (line 579)
decisions.quote: Experiment 1 was designed to replicate the counteracting effect of sugar consumption on ego depletion (Gailliot et al., 2007; Hagger et al., 2010). Following the protocol of Wang and Dvorak (2010), participants’ delay-discounting rates were assessed prior and after the consumption of a sweet drink containing either sugar or artiﬁcial sweetener.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent for this work. Both Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 (via the DG glucose-ingestion vs. SS stevia-rinse contrast on go/no-go performance, which does not use Wang and Dvorak's protocol) directly retest Gailliot et al. (2007) on whether glucose consumption counteracts ego depletion (and Experiment 1 additionally retests whether performing a self-control task lowers blood glucose levels as reported by Gailliot et al., 2007). The reference list explicitly identifies Gailliot et al. (2007), 'Self-control relies on glucose as a limited energy source. Willpower is more than a metaphor,' Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 92(2), 325-336 (DOI: 10.1037/0022-3514.92.2.325). This target is a separate work from the sole shipped row (input_row_index 2004: Wang & Dvorak, 2010, Psychological Science, DOI: 10.1177/0956797609358096) and from sibling targets 2, 3, and 4.
